mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of corporate cash flows, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of FEDFUNDS >2.0 periods, or FEDFUNDS decline reverses before 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals labor market strength, which precedes S&P 500 gains over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite consistent labor strength (PAYEMS up, UNRATE down) across 12 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates shifting supply constraints, predicting positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% while INDPRO falls over the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when the pattern persists for >3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in manufacturing production (INDPRO) below 95 for three consecutive months predicts a supply shock, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of INDPRO <95 events.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL inflation above 3% for two consecutive months triggers preemptive rate hike expectations, producing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are non-negative in >80% of CPIAUCSL >3.0 events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for 4 consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in job creation (PAYEMS), signals a tight labor market that suppresses equities over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 for 4 consecutive months and PAYEMS flat or declining
regime_hint: labor market tightness without job growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when the pattern holds for 8 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining retail activity (HOUST) while industrial production remains stable suggests a demand pullback, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for two consecutive months while INDPRO remains above 90
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative less than 10% of the time during such demand pullback episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer confidence proxies (not available in the catalog) — instead, a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 for one month followed by a rebound above 95 within the next month predicts a supply recovery and positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 90 for one month then INDPRO > 95 in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when the pattern fails to reverse within 2 months.
